newsitem.title: CANADA: GREAT-WEST UNIT NAMED IN C$80 MLN LAWSUIT.
newsitem.headline: GREAT-WEST UNIT NAMED IN C$80 MLN LAWSUIT.

text.p: Great-West Lifeco Inc's wholly owned Great-West Life Assurance Co unit was named as a defendant in an C$80 million lawsuit in an Ontario court over alleged sales of "vanishing premium" life insurance policies, plaintiffs lawyer Doug Barnett said on Thursday.

Barnett said in a statement that the suit alleged sales agents for Great-West Life Assurance "induced customers to purchase policies of life insurance based on assurances that premiums would only have to be paid for a certain number of years. But then the company returned to its customers at the end of the fixed period and asked for more money to keep the policies in force."
Great-West Lifeco could not be immediately reached for comment on the lawsuit.

Barnett said customers who could not afford to pay or refused to make payments beyond the fixed number of years may have lost the promised cash surrender value of their policies or lost some or all of their death benefits.
The lawsuit claims C$40 million in compensatory damages and C$40 million in punitive damages, Barnett's statement said.
